Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: A user wants to create a plan
    When: kspec plan add --title "Title" --content "Markdown content" is run
    Then: A plan is created with ULID, stored in project.plans.yaml, and auto-committed to shadow branch
  [ac-2]
    Given: A markdown file exists at a path
    When: kspec plan add --title "Title" --content-file ./plan.md is run
    Then: File content is read and stored as plan content
  [ac-3]
    Given: A plan exists in draft status
    When: kspec plan set @plan --status approved is run
    Then: Status is updated to approved and approved_at timestamp is set
  [ac-4]
    Given: A plan is in completed or rejected status
    When: kspec plan set @plan --status draft is run
    Then: Command fails with exit code 5 (conflict) and message Cannot transition from terminal status
  [ac-7]
    Given: Multiple plans exist in various states
    When: kspec plan list [--status <filter>] is run
    Then: Plans are listed with title, status, derived task count, and timestamps
  [ac-8]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan get @plan is run
    Then: Full plan displayed: title, status, content (markdown), linked tasks, timestamps
  [ac-9]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan note @plan "Progress note..." is run
    Then: Note is appended to plan notes array with ULID, timestamp, and author
  [ac-30]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan get @plan --json is run
    Then: Output is valid JSON with all plan fields (title, status, content, derived_tasks, timestamps)
  [ac-31]
    Given: Multiple plans exist
    When: kspec plan list --json is run

─── Description ───
Plans are durable artifacts that capture implementation context, approach, and rationale before translating to specs and tasks. They persist in the shadow branch, link to derived work, and provide auditable planning history.

─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-1]
    Given: A user wants to create a plan
    When: kspec plan add --title "Title" --content "Markdown content" is run
    Then: A plan is created with ULID, stored in project.plans.yaml, and auto-committed to shadow branch
  [ac-2]
    Given: A markdown file exists at a path
    When: kspec plan add --title "Title" --content-file ./plan.md is run
    Then: File content is read and stored as plan content
  [ac-3]
    Given: A plan exists in draft status
    When: kspec plan set @plan --status approved is run
    Then: Status is updated to approved and approved_at timestamp is set
  [ac-4]
    Given: A plan is in completed or rejected status
    When: kspec plan set @plan --status draft is run
    Then: Command fails with exit code 5 (conflict) and message Cannot transition from terminal status
  [ac-5]
    Given: An approved or active plan exists
    When: kspec plan derive @plan is run
    Then: A task is created with plan_ref pointing to the plan, the plan's derived_tasks array is updated, and plan transitions to active if not already
  [ac-6]
    Given: A task was derived from a plan
    When: kspec task get @task or kspec plan get @plan is run
    Then: Both display the bidirectional link (task shows plan_ref, plan shows derived_tasks)
  [ac-7]
    Given: Multiple plans exist in various states
    When: kspec plan list [--status <filter>] is run
    Then: Plans are listed with title, status, derived task count, and timestamps
  [ac-8]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan get @plan is run
    Then: Full plan displayed: title, status, content (markdown), linked tasks, timestamps
  [ac-9]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan note @plan "Progress note..." is run
    Then: Note is appended to plan's notes array with ULID, timestamp, and author
  [ac-10]
    Given: A task has plan_ref pointing to a non-existent plan
    When: kspec validate is run
    Then: Validation warns about dangling plan reference
  [ac-11]
    Given: A plan file with ## Specs YAML block exists
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Specs are parsed from YAML, validated against schema, and created in order (parents before children)
  [ac-12]
    Given: A plan file with derive_from_specs: true in Tasks section
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Tasks are auto-derived from each created spec, with plan_ref linking to imported plan
  [ac-13]
    Given: A plan file has ## Implementation Notes section
    When: Specs and tasks are auto-created
    Then: Implementation notes are added as initial note to all derived tasks
  [ac-14]
    Given: A plan contains a spec with slug that already exists
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run (no flags)
    Then: Existing spec is skipped with warning, other specs still created
  [ac-15]
    Given: A plan file with specs and tasks
    When: kspec plan import <path> --dry-run is run
    Then: Shows what would be created without making changes, exits with code 0
  [ac-16]
    Given: A plan with spec cli-traits that references parent @json-output (defined earlier in same plan)
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Specs are created in topological order (parents before children), local refs resolved against newly-created specs
  [ac-17]
    Given: A plan with spec referencing parent @nonexistent (not in plan, not in project)
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Error Parent @nonexistent not found, that spec is skipped, other valid specs still created
  [ac-18]
    Given: A plan where spec A has parent @B and spec B has parent @A
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Error Circular parent reference: @A -> @B -> @A, import aborts before creating specs
  [ac-19]
    Given: A plan with derive_from_specs: true and specs json-output and cli-traits
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Each derived task has spec_ref pointing to source spec AND plan_ref pointing to imported plan
  [ac-20]
    Given: A plan with derive_from_specs: true and spec titled JSON Output Mode
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Derived task has title Implement JSON Output Mode (matching kspec derive convention)
  [ac-21]
    Given: A plan file with malformed YAML in Specs section
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Error with line number and parser message, exit code 2 (USAGE)
  [ac-22]
    Given: A plan spec entry missing required title field
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Error Spec at index N missing required field: title, that spec skipped
  [ac-23]
    Given: A plan with 5 specs where 2 have errors and 3 are valid
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: 3 valid specs created, exit code 0 (success), output shows Created 3 specs, 2 errors with error details
  [ac-24]
    Given: A plan file is successfully imported
    When: Import completes
    Then: Plan record added to project.plans.yaml with status active, source path, list of created spec/task refs
  [ac-25]
    Given: A plan previously imported (specs @json-output and @cli-traits exist)
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run again
    Then: Existing specs skipped with message, no duplicates, exit code 0
  [ac-26]
    Given: A previously imported plan where @json-output has changed content
    When: kspec plan import <path> --update is run
    Then: Existing spec @json-output is updated to match plan, message Updated @json-output
  [ac-27]
    Given: A plan with additional tasks array in Tasks section (tasks without specs)
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Manual tasks are created without spec_ref, only with plan_ref
  [ac-28]
    Given: A plan has been imported with slug auth-redesign
    When: @auth-redesign is used in any kspec command
    Then: Reference resolves to the plan (ReferenceIndex includes plans)
  [ac-29]
    Given: A plan with 5 specs where 2 have validation errors
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run (default behavior)
    Then: Valid specs are created, errors logged, exit code 0 with summary output
  [ac-30]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan get @plan --json is run
    Then: Output is valid JSON with all plan fields (title, status, content, derived_tasks, timestamps)
  [ac-31]
    Given: Multiple plans exist
    When: kspec plan list --json is run
    Then: Output is JSON array of plan objects with summary fields
  [ac-32]
    Given: A plan file is imported
    When: kspec plan import <path> --json is run
    Then: Output is JSON with created specs, tasks, and any errors

    When: Error is displayed
    Then: Message includes recovery hint: Check parent exists or define it earlier in plan

First-Party Plan Support
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KGKSNZQJ7KKJ747VXPBMX9TP
Slugs:     plan-support
Type:      feature
Tags:      planning, shadow, agent-first

─── Description ───
Plans are durable artifacts that capture implementation context, approach, and rationale before translating to specs and tasks. They persist in the shadow branch, link to derived work, and provide auditable planning history.

─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-1]
    Given: A user wants to create a plan
    When: kspec plan add --title "Title" --content "Markdown content" is run
    Then: A plan is created with ULID, stored in project.plans.yaml, and auto-committed to shadow branch
  [ac-2]
    Given: A markdown file exists at a path
    When: kspec plan add --title "Title" --content-file ./plan.md is run
    Then: File content is read and stored as plan content
  [ac-3]
    Given: A plan exists in draft status
    When: kspec plan set @plan --status approved is run
    Then: Status is updated to approved and approved_at timestamp is set
  [ac-4]
    Given: A plan is in completed or rejected status
    When: kspec plan set @plan --status draft is run
    Then: Command fails with exit code 5 (conflict) and message Cannot transition from terminal status
  [ac-5]
    Given: An approved or active plan exists
    When: kspec plan derive @plan is run
    Then: A task is created with plan_ref pointing to the plan, the plan's derived_tasks array is updated, and plan transitions to active if not already
  [ac-6]
    Given: A task was derived from a plan
    When: kspec task get @task or kspec plan get @plan is run
    Then: Both display the bidirectional link (task shows plan_ref, plan shows derived_tasks)
  [ac-7]
    Given: Multiple plans exist in various states
    When: kspec plan list [--status <filter>] is run
    Then: Plans are listed with title, status, derived task count, and timestamps
  [ac-8]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan get @plan is run
    Then: Full plan displayed: title, status, content (markdown), linked tasks, timestamps
  [ac-9]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan note @plan "Progress note..." is run
    Then: Note is appended to plan's notes array with ULID, timestamp, and author
  [ac-10]
    Given: A task has plan_ref pointing to a non-existent plan
    When: kspec validate is run
    Then: Validation warns about dangling plan reference
  [ac-11]
    Given: A plan file with ## Specs YAML block exists
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Specs are parsed from YAML, validated against schema, and created in order (parents before children)
  [ac-12]
    Given: A plan file with derive_from_specs: true in Tasks section
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Tasks are auto-derived from each created spec, with plan_ref linking to imported plan
  [ac-13]
    Given: A plan file has ## Implementation Notes section
    When: Specs and tasks are auto-created
    Then: Implementation notes are added as initial note to all derived tasks
  [ac-14]
    Given: A plan contains a spec with slug that already exists
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run (no flags)
    Then: Existing spec is skipped with warning, other specs still created
  [ac-15]
    Given: A plan file with specs and tasks
    When: kspec plan import <path> --dry-run is run
    Then: Shows what would be created without making changes, exits with code 0
  [ac-16]
    Given: A plan with spec cli-traits that references parent @json-output (defined earlier in same plan)
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Specs are created in topological order (parents before children), local refs resolved against newly-created specs
  [ac-17]
    Given: A plan with spec referencing parent @nonexistent (not in plan, not in project)
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Error Parent @nonexistent not found, that spec is skipped, other valid specs still created
  [ac-18]
    Given: A plan where spec A has parent @B and spec B has parent @A
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Error Circular parent reference: @A -> @B -> @A, import aborts before creating specs
  [ac-19]
    Given: A plan with derive_from_specs: true and specs json-output and cli-traits
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Each derived task has spec_ref pointing to source spec AND plan_ref pointing to imported plan
  [ac-20]
    Given: A plan with derive_from_specs: true and spec titled JSON Output Mode
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Derived task has title Implement JSON Output Mode (matching kspec derive convention)
  [ac-21]
    Given: A plan file with malformed YAML in Specs section
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Error with line number and parser message, exit code 2 (USAGE)
  [ac-22]
    Given: A plan spec entry missing required title field
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Error Spec at index N missing required field: title, that spec skipped
  [ac-23]
    Given: A plan with 5 specs where 2 have errors and 3 are valid
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: 3 valid specs created, exit code 0 (success), output shows Created 3 specs, 2 errors with error details
  [ac-24]
    Given: A plan file is successfully imported
    When: Import completes
    Then: Plan record added to project.plans.yaml with status active, source path, list of created spec/task refs
  [ac-25]
    Given: A plan previously imported (specs @json-output and @cli-traits exist)
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run again
    Then: Existing specs skipped with message, no duplicates, exit code 0
  [ac-26]
    Given: A previously imported plan where @json-output has changed content
    When: kspec plan import <path> --update is run
    Then: Existing spec @json-output is updated to match plan, message Updated @json-output
  [ac-27]
    Given: A plan with additional tasks array in Tasks section (tasks without specs)
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run
    Then: Manual tasks are created without spec_ref, only with plan_ref
  [ac-28]
    Given: A plan has been imported with slug auth-redesign
    When: @auth-redesign is used in any kspec command
    Then: Reference resolves to the plan (ReferenceIndex includes plans)
  [ac-29]
    Given: A plan with 5 specs where 2 have validation errors
    When: kspec plan import <path> is run (default behavior)
    Then: Valid specs are created, errors logged, exit code 0 with summary output
  [ac-30]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan get @plan --json is run
    Then: Output is valid JSON with all plan fields (title, status, content, derived_tasks, timestamps)
  [ac-31]
    Given: Multiple plans exist
    When: kspec plan list --json is run
    Then: Output is JSON array of plan objects with summary fields
  [ac-32]
    Given: A plan file is imported
    When: kspec plan import <path> --json is run
    Then: Output is JSON with created specs, tasks, and any errors
  [ac-33]
    Given: Plan import encounters a missing parent reference
    When: Error is displayed
    Then: Message includes recovery hint: Check parent exists or define it earlier in plan

    When: kspec plan get @plan is run

  [ac-30]
    Given: A plan exists
    When: kspec plan get @plan --json is run
    Then: Output is valid JSON with all plan fields (title, status, content, derived_tasks, timestamps)

/**
 * Centralized error messages for CLI commands
 *
 * Organizes error messages by category to improve maintainability and consistency.
 * Each category corresponds to a common error pattern across command files.
 */

/**
 * Reference resolution errors (not found, ambiguous, wrong type)
 */
export const referenceErrors = {
  // Not found
  itemNotFound: (ref: string) => `Item not found: ${ref}`,
  taskNotFound: (ref: string) => `Task not found: ${ref}`,
  specNotFound: (ref: string) => `Spec item not found: ${ref}`,
  metaNotFound: (ref: string) => `Meta item not found: ${ref}`,
  inboxNotFound: (ref: string) => `Inbox item not found: ${ref}`,
  observationNotFound: (ref: string) => `Observation not found: ${ref}`,
  depNotFound: (ref: string) => `Dependency reference not found: ${ref}`,
  acNotFound: (acId: string, itemRef: string) =>
    `Acceptance criterion "${acId}" not found on @${itemRef}`,

  // Ambiguous references
  ambiguous: (ref: string) => `Reference "${ref}" is ambiguous. Matches:`,
  slugMapsToMultiple: (ref: string) =>
    `Slug "${ref}" maps to multiple items. Use ULID instead:`,

  // Wrong type
  notTask: (ref: string) =>
    `Reference "${ref}" is not a task (it's a spec item)`,
  notItem: (ref: string) =>
    `"${ref}" is a task, not a spec item. Use 'kspec task get' instead.`,
  taskUseTaskCommands: (ref: string) =>
    `"${ref}" is a task. Use 'kspec task' commands instead.`,
  itemUseTaskCancel: (ref: string) =>
    `"${ref}" is a task. Use 'kspec task cancel' instead.`,
  parentIsTask: (ref: string) =>
    `"${ref}" is a task. Items can only be added under spec items.`,
  notSpecItem: (ref: string) =>
    `Reference "${ref}" is a task, not a spec item. Derive only works on spec items.`,

  // Meta reference errors
  metaRefNotFound: (ref: string) => `meta_ref '${ref}' not found`,
  metaRefPointsToSpec: (ref: string) =>
    `meta_ref '${ref}' points to a spec item; use --spec-ref for product spec references`,

  // Spec reference errors
  specRefNotFound: (ref: string) => `Spec reference not found: ${ref}`,
  specRefIsTask: (ref: string) =>
    `Reference "${ref}" is a task, not a spec item`,

  // Reference not found (generic)
  refNotFound: (ref: string) => `Reference not found: ${ref}`,
} as const;

/**
 * Slug validation errors
 */
export const slugErrors = {
  alreadyExists: (slug: string, existingUlid: string) =>
    `Slug '${slug}' already exists (used by ${existingUlid})`,
  notFound: (slug: string) => `Slug '${slug}' not found on item`,
  cannotRemoveLast: (slug: string) =>
    `Cannot remove last slug '${slug}' - items must have at least one slug`,
} as const;

/**
 * Validation errors (JSON, data format, constraints)
 */
export const validationErrors = {
  // JSON parsing
  invalidJson: "Invalid JSON syntax",
  invalidJsonInData: (err: string) =>
    `Invalid JSON in --data${err ? `: ${err}` : ""}`,
  invalidJsonFromStdin: (err: string) =>
    `Invalid JSON from stdin${err ? `: ${err}` : ""}`,
  invalidPatchData: (err: string) =>
    `Invalid patch data${err ? `: ${err}` : ""}`,

  // Data validation
  noPatchesProvided: "No patches provided",
  noPatchData: "No patch data. Use --data or pipe JSON to stdin.",
  noInputProvided:
    "No input provided. Use --data for single item or pipe JSONL/JSON for bulk.",
  failedToParseBulk: (err: string) =>
    `Failed to parse bulk input${err ? `: ${err}` : ""}`,
  expectedJsonArray: "Expected JSON array",
  patchMustBeObject: (index: number) =>
    `Item ${index + 1}: Patch must be an object`,
  patchMustHaveRef: (index: number) =>
    `Item ${index + 1}: Patch must have "ref" string`,
  patchMustHaveData: (index: number) =>
    `Item ${index + 1}: Patch must have "data" object`,
  jsonLineError: (line: number, message: string) => `Line ${line}: ${message}`,

  // Field validation
  unknownFields: (fields: string[]) => `Unknown field(s): ${fields.join(", ")}`,
  invalidPatchDataWithIssues: (issues: string) =>
    `Invalid patch data: ${issues}`,

/**
 * Centralized error messages for CLI commands
 *
 * Organizes error messages by category to improve maintainability and consistency.
 * Each category corresponds to a common error pattern across command files.
 */

/**
 * Reference resolution errors (not found, ambiguous, wrong type)
 */
export const referenceErrors = {
  // Not found
  itemNotFound: (ref: string) => `Item not found: ${ref}`,
  taskNotFound: (ref: string) => `Task not found: ${ref}`,
  specNotFound: (ref: string) => `Spec item not found: ${ref}`,
  metaNotFound: (ref: string) => `Meta item not found: ${ref}`,
  inboxNotFound: (ref: string) => `Inbox item not found: ${ref}`,
  observationNotFound: (ref: string) => `Observation not found: ${ref}`,
  depNotFound: (ref: string) => `Dependency reference not found: ${ref}`,
  acNotFound: (acId: string, itemRef: string) =>
    `Acceptance criterion "${acId}" not found on @${itemRef}`,

  // Ambiguous references
  ambiguous: (ref: string) => `Reference "${ref}" is ambiguous. Matches:`,
  slugMapsToMultiple: (ref: string) =>
    `Slug "${ref}" maps to multiple items. Use ULID instead:`,

  // Wrong type
  notTask: (ref: string) =>
    `Reference "${ref}" is not a task (it's a spec item)`,
  notItem: (ref: string) =>
    `"${ref}" is a task, not a spec item. Use 'kspec task get' instead.`,
  taskUseTaskCommands: (ref: string) =>
    `"${ref}" is a task. Use 'kspec task' commands instead.`,
  itemUseTaskCancel: (ref: string) =>
    `"${ref}" is a task. Use 'kspec task cancel' instead.`,
  parentIsTask: (ref: string) =>
    `"${ref}" is a task. Items can only be added under spec items.`,
  notSpecItem: (ref: string) =>
    `Reference "${ref}" is a task, not a spec item. Derive only works on spec items.`,

  // Meta reference errors
  metaRefNotFound: (ref: string) => `meta_ref '${ref}' not found`,
  metaRefPointsToSpec: (ref: string) =>
    `meta_ref '${ref}' points to a spec item; use --spec-ref for product spec references`,

  // Spec reference errors
  specRefNotFound: (ref: string) => `Spec reference not found: ${ref}`,
  specRefIsTask: (ref: string) =>
    `Reference "${ref}" is a task, not a spec item`,

  // Reference not found (generic)
  refNotFound: (ref: string) => `Reference not found: ${ref}`,
} as const;

 * Slug validation errors
 */
export const slugErrors = {
  alreadyExists: (slug: string, existingUlid: string) =>

/**
 * Field labels and section headers used throughout the CLI output
 */

import chalk from "chalk";

/**
 * Session context section headers
 */
export const sessionHeaders = {
  title: chalk.blue.bold("=== Session Context ==="),
  activeWork: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Active Work ---"),
  noActiveWork: chalk.gray("--- No Active Work ---"),
  awaitingReview: chalk.yellow.bold("--- Awaiting Review ---"),
  recentlyCompleted: chalk.green.bold("--- Recently Completed ---"),
  recentNotes: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Recent Notes ---"),
  incompleteTodos: chalk.yellow.bold("--- Incomplete Todos ---"),
  readyTasks: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Ready to Pick Up ---"),
  blocked: chalk.red.bold("--- Blocked ---"),
  recentCommits: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Recent Commits ---"),
  inbox: chalk.magenta.bold("--- Inbox (oldest first) ---"),
  workingTree: chalk.yellow.bold("--- Working Tree ---"),
  workingTreeClean: chalk.gray("--- Working Tree: Clean ---"),
  quickCommands: chalk.gray.bold("--- Quick Commands ---"),
} as const;

/**
 * Task/Item detail field labels
 */
export const fieldLabels = {
  ulid: "ULID:",
  slugs: "Slugs:",
  type: "Type:",
  status: "Status:",
  priority: "Priority:",
  automation: "Automation:",
  maturity: "Maturity:",
  specRef: "Spec ref:",
  metaRef: "Meta ref:",
  depends: "Depends:",
  blocked: "Blocked:",
  tags: "Tags:",
  created: "Created:",
  started: "Started:",
  completed: "Completed:",
  implementation: "Implementation: ",
  description: "Description:",
  acceptanceCriteria: "Acceptance Criteria:",
  traceability: "Traceability:",
} as const;

/**
 * Output section separators
 */
export const sectionHeaders = {
  specContext: chalk.gray("─── Spec Context ───"),
  description: chalk.gray("─── Description ───"),
  acceptanceCriteria: chalk.gray("─── Acceptance Criteria ───"),
  notes: chalk.gray("─── Notes ───"),
  todos: chalk.gray("─── Todos ───"),
} as const;

/**
 * Common CLI hints/suggestions
 */
export const hints = {
  inboxPromote: chalk.gray("Use: kspec inbox promote <ref> to convert to task"),
  taskNote: (ref: string) =>
    chalk.gray(`Use: kspec task note ${ref} "<note>" to add context`),
  taskComplete: (ref: string) =>
    chalk.gray(
      `Use: kspec task complete ${ref} --reason "<summary>" when done`,
    ),
  taskStart: (ref: string) =>
    chalk.gray(`Use: kspec task start ${ref} to begin work`),
  gitCommit: chalk.gray(
    'Use: git add -A && git commit -m "..." to commit changes',
  ),
} as const;

/**
 * Summary/count messages
 */
export const summaries = {
  noTasks: chalk.gray("No tasks found"),
  taskCount: (count: number) => chalk.gray(`${count} task(s)`),
} as const;

- Implemented --plan-ref flag in task add command with validation
- Implemented --plan-ref flag in task set command (supports clearing with 'null')
- Updated task get output to display Plan ref field
- Validation ensures plan_ref points to actual plans, not tasks or spec items

- Creating tasks with plan_ref
- Displaying plan_ref in task get output
- Setting/clearing plan_ref with task set
- JSON output support
- Validation (plan exists, not pointing to task/spec)
- Handling tasks without plan_ref

All tests passing.

Task: @01KGKST6
Spec: @plan-derive

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
